narrative.overview:
Each season's robot is launched the way a hardware company launches a product: the machine alone on an almost-black stage, lit from above, standing on a thin floor line. Then the page steps out into calm white and aluminium-grey reading pages that explain the robot, the people, the outreach and the partners. Light is the accent. There is no brand hue: colour comes only from the robots, the photos, the Mercury logo (kept as-is) and the four tier metals from the 2026–27 sponsorship package.

Two grounds carry the site. The stage (home launch, every season head, the partners head, and the closing "join or partner" bands on the home, team and partners pages) and the reading ground (white, with aluminium-grey bands and tiles). Sections are separated by a change of ground, never by hairlines. Content sits on flat, filled, rounded tiles (10/14/18px), buttons are pills, and nothing casts a shadow except a robot on its floor (the only other shadows are the small lift under the chosen outreach year and the halo around the part markers). One family, Archivo, does everything; robot names are set extra wide (125%).

The neutrals are our own: tinted from the logo's dark outline, not copied. The reference study of Apple, TechCrunch, Vogue, The New York Times Company and Prada specifically warned against reusing Apple's exact greys (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) and its 28px cards, which is why the values and radii here differ.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: the near-black stage for launches and closing calls, white and aluminium grey for reading.
No brand hue; light, robots, photos, the logo and the tier metals carry all colour.
Archivo only: normal width at 600 for headings, 125% width at 700 for robot names, tabular figures for every number.
Flat filled tiles with 10/14/18px corners, pill buttons, no section hairlines, no card shadows.
Selection shown as light brightening (the chosen robot steps into a spotlight), never as a sliding bar.
One authored load moment on the stage, one scroll reveal for content, everything else answers the visitor.

rules.name: The Light Is The Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no brand colour. Emphasis on the stage is brightness (a spotlight, full colour against dimmed grey); on light pages it is ink and weight. Don't introduce a hue for links, buttons or highlights.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: The stage is for launching a machine, opening the partners page and the closing call to join or partner. Write-ups, people, records and forms sit on paper or aluminium.

rules.name: The Metals Are Swatches Rule
rules.body: The four metals appear only as tier swatches, never as text, fills or borders.

rules.name: The Width Is The Voice Rule
rules.body: Only robot and game names go wide (125%, 700). Page titles, section heads and reading text stay at normal width.

rules.name: The Fixed-Place Figures Rule
rules.body: Every date, amount, spec and result uses tabular lining figures (`<time>` and `.num` get them automatically; spec, facts, figures, budget and season-fact values set them).

rules.name: The Flat Tile Rule
rules.body: Tiles, cards, menus and panels never cast shadows and never nest. A tile is a filled rounded rectangle on a contrasting ground, nothing more.

dos: Do change colours, sizes, radii and spacing in `:root` in `css/style.css`, never in a component rule.
Do use the stage only for a launch (home, season heads), the partners head and the closing call to join or partner; put everything else on paper or aluminium.
Do put content on a filled tile in the opposite ground (aluminium on white, white on grey, Stage Step on the stage) with 14px corners.
Do make every button, toggle, tag and chip a pill; use `.btn` on light and `.btn--light` / `.btn--outline-light` on the stage.
Do set only robot and game names at 125% width and 700; keep everything else at normal width.
Do give every date, amount, spec and result tabular figures.
Do show a chosen state as light (brighter, full colour, filled dot) and write it to the URL when it is a view someone might share.
Do add a new below-the-fold block to the `reveal` selector list rather than writing a new entrance animation.
Do set `--w` to the image's pixel width on every `.photo`.
Do keep the sponsor strip in every footer, built from `SPONSORS` / `SUPPORTERS` in `js/main.js`.
Do add raster images only as the team's own photos or CAD renders, and record how any edited one was made (Assets and Provenance below).
donts: Don't add a brand hue, a purple or violet accent, or neon on black.
Don't copy Apple's exact neutrals (#F5F5F7, #A1A1A6) or its 28px cards; use the tokens here.
Don't separate sections with hairlines; change the ground instead. Lines belong inside data only.
Don't put shadows on tiles, buttons, menus or panels, or nest a tile inside a tile.
Don't use the tier metals for anything but the tier swatches.
Don't add a second font family or system display faces.
Don't put small labels (eyebrows) above headings or number the seasons 01/02/03.
Don't add new load animations outside the stage, counters that tick up, or motion that ignores reduced motion.
Don't generate or invent images, results, sponsors or numbers; leave "TBD" instead.
Don't show a photo larger than its own pixels.
